'''Phillip Crews''' (born August 15, 1943) is an African American chemist at [[University of California, Santa Cruz|UCSC]]. His research work is around [[Marine pharmacognosy|marine natural products chemistry]] and diversity education in chemistry.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=January 29, 2007|title=Phillip O. Crews - Blackpast|url=https://www.blackpast.org/african-american-history/crews-phillip-o-1943/|access-date=August 13, 2021}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2008.

== Early life ==
Crews was born in [[Champaign–Urbana metropolitan area|Champaign-Urbana]], Illinois and lived in [[Chicago]] until the family moved to Palo Alto in the 1950s.<ref name=":4" /> Crews attended Wilbur Junior High School and then [[Ellwood P. Cubberley High School|Cubberley High School]]. He next attended [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], where he received a BS in chemistry and wrote the senior thesis: “Coupling constant mechanisms in <sup>1</sup>H NMR”. He then received a PhD in chemistry at [[University of California, Santa Barbara|UCSB]] under Dominic J. Bertelli with a thesis titled “Chemistry of non-[[benzenoid]] aromatics”.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crews |first=Phillip |date=1961 |title=The question of aromaticity in non-benzenoid carbocycles : a re-evaluation of the mechanism for the silver catalyzed addition of benzyne to polyenes |url=https://worldcat.org/en/title/1176032156}}</ref> Crews then wrote and was awarded an NSF postdoctoral fellowship to investigate the [[stereochemistry]] of organo-metalloids at [[Princeton University]] with the late [[Kurt Mislow]].<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Citation |last1=Rodríguez |first1=Jaime |chapter=Contemporary Strategies in Natural Products Structure Elucidation |date=2012 |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-90-481-3834-0_7 |title=Handbook of Marine Natural Products |pages=423–517 |editor-last=Fattorusso |editor-first=Ernesto |place=Dordrecht |publisher=Springer Netherlands |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-90-481-3834-0_7 |isbn=978-90-481-3834-0 |access-date=2022-10-21 |last2=Crews |first2=Phillip |last3=Jaspars |first3=Marcel |editor2-last=Gerwick |editor2-first=William H. |editor3-last=Taglialatela-Scafati |editor3-first=Orazio|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Research ==
In 1970, Crews obtained a position in the chemistry department at [[University of California, Santa Cruz|UCSC]], where he began his research career investigating [[physical organic chemistry]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1973 he shifted his research program towards the nascent area of [[Marine pharmacognosy|marine natural products chemistry]]<ref>{{Cite news|last=Krajick|first=Kevin|date=April 30, 2004|title=Medicine from the Sea: From slime to sponges, scientists are plumbing the ocean's depths for new medications to treat cancer, pain and other ailments|work=Smithsonian Magazine|url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/medicine-from-the-sea-99586066/|access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=BORG|first=JAMES C.|date=June 13, 1988|title=Sea Cure : Scientists Enthusiastic About Potential Medical Compounds From Deep|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1988-06-13-me-3212-story.html|access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Petkewich|first=Rachel|date=May 2007|title=Taking The Familiar Route: Pharma Still Has Room For Natural Products Chemists|work=Chemical and Engineering News|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/85/i20/Taking-Familiar-Route.html|access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref> as an untenured assistant professor.

Crews uses bioassay-guided isolation to discover natural products that may help treat or cure human diseases, incorporating elements of structure elucidation and employing state-of-the-art nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Wines & winemaking Merging Chemistry Fundamentals and Sensory Evaluation Outcomes to Gain a 21st Century Perspective|url=https://www.brownpapertickets.com/event/4071149|access-date=September 7, 2021}}</ref> He became especially interested in the molecular structures of the [[psymberin]]s and the bengamides, molecules isolated from Indo-Pacific sponges.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Cichewicz|first1=Robert H.|last2=Cragg|first2=Gordon M.|last3=Linington|first3=Roger G.|last4=Wright|first4=Amy E.|year=2017|title=Special Issue in Honor of Professor Phil Crews - ACS|journal=Journal of Natural Products|volume=80|issue=3|pages=579–581|doi=10.1021/acs.jnatprod.7b00161|pmid=28335607|doi-access=free}}</ref> [[Psymberin]] is one of his most important discoveries because of its potential for further development to treat solid tumor cancers. The mixed [[Nonribosomal peptide|NRPS]]-PKS biosynthetic product comes from the marine sponge ''Psammocinia'' aff''. Bulbosa''. Crews research on psymberin has stimulated almost 100 studies and publications by other laboratories. Another molecule of importance is bengamide B, that led to an anti-cancer Phase I clinical trial on a close analog.<ref name=":4" /> 
In addition to these two molecules, Crews has discovered many small molecule tools derived from marine sponges, some of which are used worldwide by research teams as molecular probes.  These small molecules include the [[Cytoskeletal drugs|actin inhibitors]], jasplakinolide and [[latrunculin]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Amagata|first1=Taro|last2=Johnson|first2=Tyler A.|last3=Cichewicz|first3=Robert H.|last4=Tenney|first4=Karen|last5=Mooberry|first5=Susan L.|last6=Media|first6=Joseph|last7=Edelstein|first7=Matthew|last8=Valeriote|first8=Frederick A.|last9=Crews|first9=Phillip|date=2008-11-27|title=Interrogating the Bioactive Pharmacophore of the Latrunculin Chemotype by Investigating the Metabolites of Two Taxonomically Unrelated Sponges|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/jm8008585|journal=Journal of Medicinal Chemistry|volume=51|issue=22|pages=7234–7242|doi=10.1021/jm8008585|issn=0022-2623|pmc=2772107|pmid=18942825}}</ref> the [[Mitochondrial complex I|Mitochondrial Complex I]] inhibitor, mycothiazole, the human methionine aminopeptidase inhibitor, and fascaplysins, an opioid receptor agonist. He is also a holder of a patent for oxazole anthelmintic agents of marine origin.<ref>{{Cite web|title=US Patent for Oxazole anthelmintic agents of marine origin|url=https://patents.justia.com/patent/4785012|access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref> 
Crews led and co-authored of the widely-used textbook, “Organic Structure Analysis”.,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Organic Structure Analysis - Hardcover - Phillip Crews; Jaime Rodriguez; Marcel Jaspars - Oxford University Press|url=https://global.oup.com/ushe/product/organic-structure-analysis-9780195336047?cc=us&lang=en&|access-date=2021-08-12|website=global.oup.com}}</ref> along with Marcel Jaspars and Jaime Rodriguez. The first edition was published by Oxford University Press in 1998 and with the second edition being published in 2009. Crews' goal was to highlight the intense complexity of spectroscopic analysis of natural products, from which the “Crews rule” emerged. The “Crews rule” states that if a molecule’s ratio of hydrogens to carbons is less than 1, then additional measures should be performed to confirm the structure.<ref name=":4" />

In 1990 he became the principal investigator in the National Cooperative Drug Discovery Group (NCDDG) program.,<ref>{{Cite web|title=National Cooperative Drug Discovery/Development Groups (NCDDG) for the Treatment of Mental Disorders, Drug or Alcohol Addiction (U19)|url=https://www.federalgrants.com/National-Cooperative-Drug-Discovery-Development-Groups-NCDDG-for-the-Treatment-of-Mental-Disorders-Drug-or-Alcohol-Addiction-U19-46172.html|access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref> a position he held for 20 years.<ref name=":4" /> In 2017, he was honored with a special issue of the ''Journal of Natural Products.''<ref name=":4" />

== Diversity and outreach ==
Crews has participated and led in numerous outreach programs,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Project 5-215 Indonesia|url=https://sites.nationalacademies.org/PGA/PEER/PEERscience/PGA_174196|access-date=November 5, 2021|website=National Academies of Science, Engineering, and Medicine. Partnerships for Enhanced Engagement in Research (PEER)}}</ref> including running the NIH-supported ACCESS program<ref>{{Cite web|title=A C C E S S :: Home|url=http://access.ucsc.edu/|access-date=2021-08-12|website=access.ucsc.edu}}</ref> for the past 27 years. This program helps first-generation and under-represented students from 2-year community colleges transition to 4-year university by giving them access to cutting edge research and building their confidence to continue in careers in science. His dedication to diversity and inclusion was recognized with UCSC's 2004 Excellence through Diversity Award.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|last=Donahue|first=Louise|date=June 24, 2004|title=Awards honor 'excellence through diversity'|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2004/06/522.html|access-date=August 13, 2021}}</ref> He also gave the UCSC Spring 2019 Emeriti Lecture on “Inspirational Biomolecules from Oceania.”<ref>{{Cite web|title=Phil Crews Emeriti Lecture Apr 9, 2019| website=[[YouTube]] | date=June 13, 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LLauyOsakO0|access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref>
In 2021, the UCSC chemistry department established the Phillip Crews symposium, "Powered by Chemistry, Strengthened by Diversity"<ref>{{Cite web|title=Phillip Crews Symposium: Powered by Chemistry, Strengthened by Diversity|url=http://ucsc-expghost.imodules.com/controls/email_marketing/view_in_browser.aspx?sid=1069&gid=1001&sendId=2782738&ecatid=21&puid=515a2631-9fd9-46ce-81cb-fa6e42d7c70a}}</ref> and student fellowship.

== Winery ==
In Crews’ early days in academia, Crews wanted to add a new dimension to chemical education at UCSC by contributing to the general education curriculum. He therefore launched of a new course, “''Chemistry of wine - Introductory lecture-laboratory course for non-chemistry students''”<ref>{{Cite journal|title=The Chemistry of Wine. An Introductory Lecture--Laboratory Course for Nonchemistry Students.|year=1977|doi=10.1021/ED054P630|s2cid=95858110|last1=Crews|first1=Phillip|journal=Journal of Chemical Education|volume=54|issue=10|page=630|bibcode=1977JChEd..54..630C}}</ref> as well as other lectures such as Wines & winemaking Merging Chemistry Fundamentals and Sensory Evaluation Outcomes to Gain a 21st Century Perspective at [[Cabrillo College]].<ref name=":5" /> This coursework, as well as his keen interest in wine, lead him to found Pelican Ranch Winery<ref>{{Cite web|title=CRUSH TIME AT PELICAN RANCH WINERY|url=https://ksqd.org/crush-time-at-pelican-ranch-winery/|access-date=November 5, 2021|website=KSQD Community Radio|date=October 16, 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Pelican Ranch Winery {{!}} Premium Wines|url=https://pelicanranch.com/|access-date=2021-08-12|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Walker|first=Tara Fatemi|date=May 1, 2018|title=Quick Bites: Wine futurology at Pelican Ranch Winery|work=Santa Cruz Sentinel|url=https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/2018/05/01/quick-bites-wine-futurology-at-pelican-ranch-winery/|access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref> with his wife Peggy (BW CA-W-3444) in 1997.

* 2008 Elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Stephens |first1=Tim |last2=Writer 459-2495 |first2=Staff |title=Three UCSC professors elected AAAS Fellows |url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2008/12/2641.html |access-date=2022-10-21 |website=UC Santa Cruz News |language=en}}</ref>

* 2012 American Society of Pharmacognosy Fellow<ref>{{Cite web|title=ASP Fellows|url=https://www.pharmacognosy.us/what-is-pharmacognosy/the-asp-fellows/|access-date=November 5, 2021}}</ref>
* 2014 American Society of Pharmacognosy President & Vice President<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Past Presidents of the ASP - The American Society of Pharmacognosy|url=https://www.pharmacognosy.us/what-is-pharmacognosy/past-presidents-of-the-asp/|access-date=August 13, 2021}}</ref>
* 2015 Edward A. Dickson Endowed Professorship award<ref>{{Cite news|last=Stephens|first=Tim|date=August 19, 2015|title=Dickson Emeriti Professorship awarded to chemist Phil Crews|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2015/08/crews-dickson-prof.html}}</ref>
*2017 Special Issue of Journal Natural Products in Honor of Professor Phil Crews<ref name=":4" />
